correctness.rationale: The derivative ratio of two shifted-power decays has logarithmic derivative with affine numerator; therefore two different background-adjusted intensities cross at most three times, and same-background intensities at most twice. Ordered zero integrals force distinct roots. A four-function generalized Chebyshev argument proves nonsingular Jacobians; three-/two-column restrictions and the implicit function theorem prove minimality. Exact rational factorization attains both crossing limits. The standalone checker additionally confirms 1,050 finite evaluations; no finite test is used for infinite proof.

evidence: An explicit proof here shows the derivative ratio has affine logarithmic-derivative numerator and at most one turning point.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-finding corpus and primary-literature comparisons found no same or dominating exact four-bin Omori identifiability theorem. Earlier primary sources establish the model and likelihood estimators, whereas the new proof gives sharp deterministic arbitrary-bin injectivity, a known-background observation count reduction, and the attained crossing bound. Historical novelty remains provisional against unlocated general Chebyshev-system theorems.

value.rationale: The 2015 Kanto seismic model combines uncertain constant background and modified Omori aftershock intensity, and earthquake records are naturally aggregated in irregular time bins. The theorem provides a universal, sharp structural minimum of four arbitrary disjoint expected-count windows, with a strict one-window reduction if background is known, local nonsingularity and a constructive three-agreement ambiguity. Unlike generic parameter counting it proves global uniqueness and sharp nonuniqueness under arbitrary window geometry. The idealized nature and ill-conditioning limits are explicit.
